      PUBLIC INPUT
        1. Two 15-minute Public Input sessions will be allowed during each Council
           Meeting. Time will be divided equally among those wishing to speak, however,
           no person will be allowed to speak for more than 5 minutes.
                   Anyone requesting auxiliary aids or services is asked to contact
                the Administration Department five business days prior to the meeting.
                                                                                              Page 2 of 113
2. No person may address the council more than twice on any issue in any
   meeting. Comments must be addressed to the Chair and must not be personal
   or derogatory about any other person.
3. Any questions must be directly related to the topic being discussed and must
   be addressed to the Chair only, who after consultation with Council and Town
   Administrator, will determine if the question can be answered at that time.
   Questions cannot be directed to an individual Councilor and must not be
   personal in nature. Issues raised during Public Input, which cannot be resolved
   or answered at that time, or which require additional discussion or research,
   will be noted by the Town Administrator who will be responsible for researching
   and responding to the comment directly during normal work hours or by
   bringing to the Council for discussion at a subsequent meeting. The Chair
   reserves the right to end questioning if the questions depart from clarification to
   deliberation.
4. Council members may request a comment be added to New Business at a
   subsequent meeting.
5. No one may speak during Public Input except the person acknowledged by the
   Chair. Direct questions or comments from the audience are not permitted
   during Public Input.

      the Administration Department five business days prior to the meeting.

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:               Town Council
Title:            Adjustment of Hooksett Village Water Precinct Boundaries per RSA 52:1, 5 Village
                  Districts. Mike Heidorn and Commissioners from the HVWP will be available to
                  answer any related questions. This item was tabled on April 10, 2024, and on April
                  24, 2024 was postponed.


Meeting:       Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:    Community Development
Staff Contact: Bruce Thomas, Town Engineer

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The Hooksett Village Water Precinct (HVWP) wishes to confirm the limits of their service area
boundaries to more accurately depict those boundaries at the parcel level and facilitate Town
development, planning and engineering activities. No new infrastructure expansion is included. A
plan of the current service area is provided.

Per State requirements, the HVWP has petitioned and obtained the signatures of at least 10 Precinct
voters to approve of the service area boundary delineation. The Petition dated February 27, 2024 is
attached. Statutes require that the Petition be ratified by the Precinct’s voters prior to it taking effect.
To that end, it was approved at the HVWP’s Annual Meeting held on February 27, 2024. A copy of
the meeting minutes (Petition info is near the end) is attached.

At this time, the Petition must now be submitted to Town Council for consideration. The HVWP is
requesting that the Town Council approve the Petition after holding a duly-noticed public hearing, in
accordance with State requirements.

If TC approval is granted, documentation of that approval needs to occur in the records of the Town
and Precinct within 60 days of the approval.

A description of the boundaries of the Precinct’s current service area is attached. As shown on
“HVWP Service Area, Hooksett, NH” attached hereto.

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
None

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
None

RECOMMENDATION:


                                                                                                      Page 5 of 113
                                                                                   Agenda Item #11.1.


Approve of the HVWP Boundary changes as presented by the Hooksett Village Water Precinct.

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Motion to approve of the HVWP Boundary changes as presented by the Hooksett Village Water
Precinct.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
I concur with the suggested motion.

               and Vice-Chair
Meeting:       Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:    Community Development
Staff Contact: Elizabeth Robidoux, Town Planner

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
Master Plan will be presented by Planning Board Chair and Vice-Chair. It is the duty of every
Planning Board, as established by RSA 673:1, to prepare and amend a master plan to guide the
growth and development of the municipality. The master plan acts as a guide for the future. It
identifies the most appropriate future development of the community and aids the Planning Board in
designing ordinances that achieve the Master Plan’s vision and result in smart growth, sound
planning and wise resource protection.

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         Ken Conaty on behalf of the Sewer Commission Request for Sewer Easements on
               Depot Road
Meeting:       Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: Geraldine Ciardelli, Executive Assistant

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The current force main from Martin’s Ferry pump station runs in the railroad right of way on the
eastern side of the tracks. It was constructed in 1968 of single 8500’ 6” cast iron pipe. Over the years
corrosion has occurred both inside and outside the pipe. The internal corrosion is causing significant
flow losses due to friction. Another issue is the location of the pipe near the Merrimack River. Any
break in the pipe would result in raw wastewater being spilled into the river. The issues with the pipe
and its location were brought to light when we started doing hydraulic calculations for the upgrade at
Martin’s Ferry pump station to accept wastewater flow from the southern area of the TIF district
around Exit 10.

Solution:
It was determined that the best solution to these problems would be to replace the force main. We
looked at replacing it in the same location along the railroad but that may not serve as a long-term
solution if commuter rail were established, and a second rail would be need as the distance to the
new line would be minimal and access not easy.
         The new force main would be directionally drilled from the pump station approximately 4500’
feet to a spot where gravity sewer could resume. The pipe will be 8” HDPE which has a very low
friction loss resulting in much higher pumping volumes to allow the expansion of the TIF district.
Relocating the line as indicated through the western edge of the former Manchester Sand property is
the best scenario for environmental and access reasons. This line would cross the following lots:
      29 Lehoux Dr-Map 24 Lot 33- Maclellan
      25 Lehoux Dr-Map 24 Lot 32-Old Castle
      21 Lehoux Dr-Map 24 Lot 36-Public Service (formerly Manchester Sand)
      Off Depot Rd- Map 30 Lot 57-Town of Hooksett
      57 Martin’s Ferry Rd- Map 33 Lot 2- SNHU
      75 Martin’s Ferry Rd-Map 29 Lot 34- SNHU
      Off Depot Rd- Map 29 Lot 81- Town of Hooksett

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
No financial impact

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:

STAFF REPORT

To:            Town Council
Title:         $275.00 check from HealthTrust to the Town of Hooksett for the 2023 Wellness
               Coordinator Stretch Goals Earning Incentive per RSA 31:95-b, III (b)
Meeting:       Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:    Administration
Staff Contact: Donna Fitzpatrick, Human Resource Coordinator

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
HealthTrust provides healthcare coverage to New Hampshire public sector employees. The Town of
Hooksett ("Town") contracts with HealthTrust for the Town's medical (Anthem) and dental (Delta)
coverage. As a HealthTrust member, they provide the Town "Wellness Coordinator Stretch Goals".
Those stretch goals achieved by our Town result in earning incentives. Hooksett achieved the
following 2023 stretch goals:

   1. Medication Safety Program Participants: This program provides an employee a DNA testing to
      determine how safe and effective current or future medications are for him/her. These genetic
      tests can help pharmacists and providers make better choices for an employee. Town 2023
      "stretch goal" 11 and actual 17 participants = $200
   2. Targeted Wellness Trainings: This program is for a HealthTrust Wellness Advisor to present a
      health related subject to Town employees/officials. HealthTrust presented: "Medication Safety
      Program" at our annual September health fair AND "2023 Stewardship Report" to the Town
      Administrator and Human Resources Coordinator to identify top medical claims for a)
      continued employee education incentives for Smartshopper (monetary rewards for
      consumerism for cost-effective choices) and b) future plan designs to best meet Hooksett's
      goals/needs. Town 2023 "stretch goal" 1 and actual 2 = $75

FINANCIAL IMPACT:
Wellness Campaign costs are taken out of Wellness Account #001-000.2220.029.000.

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
n/a

RECOMMENDATION:
Accept $275.00 check from HealthTrust to the Town of Hooksett for the 2023 Wellness Coordinator
Stretch Goals Earning Incentive per RSA 31:95-b, III (b).

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Accept $275.00 check from HealthTrust to the Town of Hooksett for the 2023 Wellness Coordinator
Stretch Goals Earning Incentive per RSA 31:95-b, III (b).

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:              Town Council
Title:           Repair of Park's fields and funding - HYAA and the Town of Hooksett DPW
Meeting:         Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:      Administration
Staff Contact:   Geraldine Ciardelli, Executive Assistant

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
On April 10, 2024, Brian Soucy of the Hooksett Youth Athletic Association requested the Town look
into the repair of the fields, mainly at Donati and Peters brook. Brian obtained a quote for new 12,000
turf at $14,000. He requests a financial agreement and partnership with the Town with both parties
making financial contributions.

DPW has concerns as follows:

General Field Items

      Field usage has increased significantly over the years in the quantity of kids, tournament sizes
       being held, and additional seasons.
           o Flag Football used to only be in the fall which allowed the fields to be repaired and rest
              during the spring and summer. Flag football is now played in the spring and fall leaving
              the fields to rest from mid June to the end of August.
           o Soccer has been played during the spring and fall only leaving the fields to rest from
              mid June to the end of August.

      From experience of the P&R staff, putting sod down around the high traffic areas only lasted 2
       years of playing before it needed replacement again. There is just not enough time for the
       grass to rest and recover with the amount of playing time experienced on the fields.

      The report submitted by the UNH Extension suggested overseeding bare spots on the fields
       but also identified that when doing this the fields need to get “a season off” meaning no sports
       to be played until the following year. This should be considered as overseeding is the most
       economical way to repair the fields, but HYAA would most likely take issue due to the number
       of teams that need field time for daily practice and games. Also, the timeframe for overseeding
       as indicated should be done in May or September / early October. The current schedule for the
       various sports puts any overseeding right at the same time and would not allow grass a
       chance to establish themselves and would not benefit the playing field.

Financial Aspects


                                                                                                 Page 49 of 113
                                                                                        Agenda Item #15.1.


      I have reviewed the remaining budget for this fiscal year 2023-2024 with the P&R crew chief
       and feel that we do not have the funds available within the P&R Grounds Maintenance line to
       contribute towards the proposed sodding of the flag football fields at Donati.
      Budget year 2024-2025 is still to be finalized due to the default budget but we were not
       anticipating to have any additional expenses for sodding in the operating budget.
      Budget planning for year 2025-2026 will be starting in July and an increased operating budget
       could be requested and planned for. A plan would need to be put together for desired scope of
       sodding each year and what the end result that is desired. For example, repair soccer fields
       one year and repair flag football fields the next year….
      Depending on the scope of Sodding desired, maybe a warrant article would be best to fund
       this project in conjunction with HYAA
      Currently the town does not directly charge HYAA for use of the fields. The town should
       consider a fee associated with the use of the fields. The revenue generated by fees could be
       applied to any re-sodding that may be required.


FINANCIAL IMPACT:
TBD

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
TBD

RECOMMENDATION:
Review, discuss possible recommendations

SUGGESTED MOTION:
Review, discuss possible recommendations

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
Review, discuss possible recommendations

STAFF REPORT

To:              Town Council
Title:           2024-2025 Town Council Meeting Schedule
Meeting:         Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:      Administration
Staff Contact:   Geraldine Ciardelli, Executive Assistant

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
The Town Council meeting schedule is based on the fiscal year. Per Town Charter Section 3.5 c
"regular meetings (minimum one per month". Per Town Council Rules of Procedure Section 3.a (The
Council shall meet in regular session on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of every month, except as noted
on Town Calendar, at 6:00pm.")

Per Town Council Rules of Procedure Section 2.a "The Town Administrator shall act in the role of
Council Chair from July 1st until such time the new Town Council has their first meeting to choose
their Chair, Vice Chair and a Secretary. The Town Administrator, as acting Council Chair, shall lead
this meeting through Town Council Reorganization - Part I." The first meeting in July will be July 10,
2024.

Per Town Council Rules of Procedure Section 3.e "The Council may meet for an informal workshop
session or special meeting by Council vote on an as needed basis, in accordance of Section 3.5 C of
the Town Charter. The Place of meeting shall be the Council Chambers." A Workshop is scheduled
for August 14, 2025.

Additional meetings occur in September, January and February due to budgets/warrants.

Meetings in November and December scheduled in accordance with holiday season.

**The Finance Director also created the additional timelines for the Council showing Charter
Amendment Timeline and Budget Timeline.

Town Council
STAFF REPORT

To:              Town Council
Title:           Town Administrator Evaluation Review
Meeting:         Town Council - 08 May 2024
Department:      Administration
Staff Contact:   Geraldine Ciardelli, Executive Assistant

BACKGROUND INFORMATION:
PROCEDURE FOR TOWN ADMINISTRATOR ANNUAL EVALUATION

a. Council’s first meeting in May – Council will receive Town Administrator’s self-evaluation to include
status on his/her goals with comments for period ending June 30th of the same fiscal year along with
a blank evaluation form. (May 8, 2024)

b. Council’s second meeting in May- Councilors are to have completed and submitted their town
administrators evaluation form via e-mail to the council chair designated Town Administration staff
member prior to, or are to hand deliver it at the beginning of the meeting. Councilors and the
designee will then discuss in non-public, the evaluations and will finalize them into one report by a
simple majority vote. Only town councilors and the designee will be in attendance during this non-
public session to discuss and finalize the evaluation of the Town Administrator. The Town
Administrator will receive the evaluation from the council at this meeting. (May 22, 2024)

c. Council’s first meeting in June - Council will discuss the evaluation report with the Town
Administrator. (June 12, 2024)

d. Annually at the first meeting in July the Administrator’s goals will be an agenda item. The Council
and the Administrator shall define such goals and performance objectives which they determine
necessary for the proper operation of the Town and the attainment of the Council’s policy objectives
and shall further establish a relative priority among those various goals and objectives, said goals and
objectives to be reduced in writing. They shall generally be attainable within the time limitations as
specified and the annual operating capital budgets and evaluation. If goals s are not concluded, the
Council will hold a special meeting a week later to finalize the goals.

POLICY IMPLICATIONS:
Amend the Rules of Procedure and follow the Town Council Rules of Procedures above

RECOMMENDATION:
Approve update to Section 14b as amended above. Review the procedure for Town Administrator's
review and prepare.

SUGGESTED MOTION:


                                                                                                 Page 105 of 113
                                                                                     Agenda Item #16.3.


Motion to approve amended Rules of Procedure 14b as amended above. Review and follow the
procedure for Town Administrator's review and prepare.

TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S RECOMMENDATION:
Approve the amended Rules of Procedure. Town Administrator's self-evaluation submitted.

55   L. Mclaughlin- During the Town Council meeting held on March 27, 2024, the Council requested further
56   details concerning the duration and expenses involved in engaging our legal counsel to carry out
57   additional tasks necessary for finalizing closures. As of April 1, 2024, the Town has incurred $4,370.54
58   in legal fees and administrative costs. However, through the sale of the properties, $3,228 of these
59   expenses were recuperated. This leaves an outstanding amount of $1,142.54, attributable to
60   properties selling below their tax obligations and the interpleader process. This does not include staff
61   time totaling approximately 10 hours working with legal counsel, researching and supplying previous
62   owner names and addresses and lienholder information as well as contacting a previous owner to issue
63   funds due to them. The primary challenge with the Phase III properties lies in the requirement for
64   comprehensive title examinations, each of which would potentially cost in excess of $2,000. Estimating
65   these costs accurately is difficult as they depend on the time invested by legal professionals. The Town
66   would need to cover these expenses upfront, hoping to recover them post-sale. Moreover, given the
67   default budget for FY 2024-2025, allocating funds from the legal budget for this purpose poses a risk,
68   with no guarantee of reimbursement.
69
70   J. Durand motioned to hire JS Auction’s for Phase 3 of Town auctions of property; seconded by

234   TOWN ADMINISTRATOR'S REPORT- Andre Garron
235
236      •   Beautify Hooksett day- April 20th Recap- On what started out to be a raw gloomy day, Saturday
237          4-20-24, turned out to be nothing but bright and glorious day for the Hooksett Community. As
238          more than 150 registered volunteers from various Service Organizations, Scouts, local
239          businesses, churches as well as friends and neighborhood groups. “Teamed Up to Clean-Up”, as
240          part of the third annual, “Beautify Hooksett Day”. There were over 20 teams who cleaned up
241          the roadsides. Additionally, Donati Park and Lambert Park were both cleaned up. The Kiwanis
242          Club organized clean-up along Heads Pond Trail and the Conservation Commission organized
243          clean-up and were assisted by Park & Rec Dept., along the recently completed Riverwalk Trail.
244          Everyone’s hard work was rewarded after at social gathering at Lambert Park where they were
245          treated to Wood Fired Pizzas from New England TapHouse, sandwiches from Robie’s Store and
246          before their day of hard work was kicked-off with Coffee and wonderful Cider donuts from “The
247          Roadside Common Man”. The Town Recycle Center folks did an outstanding job helping to
248          organize all the logistics for this event.
249      •   Employee Appreciation Luncheon was held, we had a good turnout and I appreciate the council
250          for putting this on. The treats were provided by Cake Fairy.
251
252      D. Fitzpatrick- we kicked off our Spring Wellness Challenge, this year’s contest will be “it takes a
253      village” where employees can paint and decorate their bird houses. The boxes also include a small
254      snack and a rock with a motivational message on it, a water proof fanny pack, and more.
255
256      •   Wastewater Dept- The Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF) is proud to recognize clean
257          water projects that demonstrate excellence through the George F. Ames Performance and
258          Innovation in the SRF Creating Environmental Success (PISCES) program. These projects
259          promote EPA’s mission of protecting human health and the environment and exemplify the
260          innovative, flexible, and collaborative nature of the program. (Message from Andrew Sawyer,
261          PH.D, Director-Office of Wastewater Management). Hooksett Wastewater Department was
262          recognized by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for its Wastewater Treatment
263          Facility Phase 3 Capital Improvement Project.
264
265      •   The Planning Board adopted the 2024-2034 Master Plan on April 15, 2024. I congratulate the
266          Planning Board and Town Planner, Elizabeth Robideaux.
267
268      •   The Town Planner Position is currently open, our current Town Planner will be resigning in
269          August. We will be looking at the position and advertising soon.
270
271      •   NHDOT will close Donati Bridge on April 29, 2024, for Maintenance. The Town Council agreed
272          to NHDOT request for full closure of the bridge on April 10, 2024.
